_about: Player businesses: places on the map with a player's name on them. There is no server, so a business only shows on everyone's map once it is listed here (Eko or Nib add it). Tracks: Books (the business's own credits and debt, kept apart from the owner's), Rep (how the neighborhood treats the place), Exposure (Heat that sticks to the building). Commons protection: a Commons-clean business is left out of cops-and-robbers; corporate-funded places never have it; it breaks when an owner's Heat reaches the threshold or their Standing tips toward a corporation. Loss ladder: trouble, notice, shuttered, lost. Rules and numbers are drafts by Eko (status: draft). Roster doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/4Y8jEd8NjboEdymKjwSSxW

tracks.books: The business's own credits and debt, kept apart from the owner's personal money.
tracks.rep: How the neighborhood treats the place: regulars, events, how the owner handles trouble.
tracks.exposure: Heat that sticks to the building, not the owner: inspections, compliance notices, jobs run out of the back room.

keeps: Patch grid repair, generator fixes, feeding people
Crownline compliance fines for surviving wrong
loses: Underground jobs run from the building
protection.restore: Make it even: Exposure back to zero, Commons Standing repaired, and a favor that fits the harm.

loss.name: Trouble
loss.when: Books in debt, Rep falling or Exposure rising
loss.what: Mail warns the owner what is wrong and what fixes it.

loss.name: Notice
loss.when: Three weeks of unpaid commercial rent, or Exposure at 4
loss.what: A landlord letter, an inspection or a compliance fine.

loss.name: Shuttered
loss.what: Doors closed, stock frozen, pin marked closed. Reopens by clearing the debt, passing the inspection or winning a Public Advocacy appeal.

loss.name: Lost
loss.when: A Heat 6 crisis aimed at the business, or four weeks shuttered
loss.what: The place goes to an NPC or rival. Its pin keeps a history line, and buying it back is a story to chase.

rules.seasonClose: Owners can close for the season when they're away: rent and trouble pause.

economy._about: Draft numbers: the rulebook has no business economy. Small on purpose: the fun is the place, not the money.

offers._about: Back-room offers: one may arrive each week at an open business. Saying no costs nothing. Saying yes pays well, adds Exposure to the building and ends Commons protection until it's made even.

list.title: One night in the basement
list.body: A friend of a friend needs your back room for one night. No questions, no lights, no names.

list.title: Hold a crate
list.body: A sealed crate, three days, behind your counter. Someone collects it. You never looked inside.

list.title: Write some receipts
list.body: Someone needs a stack of receipts that say they bought things here. They didn't.

list.title: Move some stock
list.body: A box of very nice parts, cheap, no paperwork. Sell them over the counter and split the take.

list.title: Neutral ground
list.body: Two crews want to meet somewhere nobody owns. They picked you. Close early and stay out of the room.

list.title: Share your power
list.body: A neighbor's operation needs more power than it should. A cable through your wall, unofficially.

list.title: Forget a face
list.body: If anyone asks, you never saw the person in this photo come through your door last night.

list.title: A standing drop
list.body: Underground couriers want to use your place as a drop point, every week, indefinitely.

trouble.title: Trouble at {business}
trouble.body: Something's off at {business}: {why}. Fix it before it becomes a notice.

notice.title: Notice: {business}
notice.body: {business} has a formal notice: {why}. Clear it within a week or the doors close.

shuttered.title: {business} is shuttered
shuttered.body: The doors are closed and the stock is frozen. Clear the books, bring Exposure under 4, or win a Public Advocacy appeal, then reopen. Left shuttered for four weeks, it's lost.

lost.title: {business} is gone
lost.body: {business} belongs to someone else now. The sign is new. The regulars still say it used to be yours. Buying it back is a story worth chasing.

protectionLost.title: The neighborhood noticed
protectionLost.body: Word got round about what happened at {business}. The Commons won't keep trouble off your doorstep until you make it even.

protectionBack.title: Square with the neighborhood
protectionBack.body: You made it even. The Commons looks after {business} again.
